canonicalization_notes: 'Prolif Invasive Tumor' and 'Invasive Tumor' were grounded against tumor epithelial / proliferative tumor compartment literature.
'Macrophages 1' and 'Macrophages 2' were collapsed to a macrophage/TAM compartment.
'DCIS 1' and 'DCIS 2' were collapsed to DCIS literature terms.

coverage_notes: Exact PubMed pair-level support is strongest for SPP1-CD44 and VEGFA-FLT1.
TGFB1-TGFBR2 is supported through breast-cancer TGFβ/TGFBR2 stromal-axis papers rather than many exact same-title pair hits.
Canonical cell-type coverage is complete after collapsing the repo's custom labels to PubMed-standard terms.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics in breast cancer reveals tumour microenvironment-driven drug responses and clonal therapeutic heterogeneity
papers.evidence_summary: Breast cancer spatial transcriptomics identified tumor, interphase, and microenvironment regions with distinct drug-response states and unique ligand-receptor programs, directly supporting a spatial CCI framing for the current analysis.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds the use of spatially resolved ligand-receptor programs to interpret proliferative tumor regions and their surrounding microenvironment.

papers.title: Spatially and functionally distinct subclasses of breast cancer-associated fibroblasts revealed by single cell RNA sequencing
papers.evidence_summary: Single-cell profiling resolved multiple spatially separated breast cancer-associated fibroblast states with distinct origins and functions.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Supports collapsing the repo's stromal labels into a CAF/stromal compartment with heterogeneous functions in breast cancer.

papers.title: Study on the mechanism of heterogeneous tumor-associated macrophages in three subtypes of breast cancer through the integration of single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro experiments

lr_support.note: Paper explicitly reports SPP1-CD44 among TAM-associated L-R pairs in breast cancer.
Paper explicitly reports VEGFA-VEGFR1/Flt1 communication in breast cancer TAM programs.

papers.evidence_summary: Across luminal, HER2, and triple-negative breast cancer, heterogeneous TAM states showed subtype-specific communication, including VEGFA-VEGFR1, SPP1-CD44, and SPP1-ITGB1 interactions.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: This is the cleanest direct PubMed support for two of the target L-R pairs in a breast-cancer immune-microenvironment setting.

papers.title: Breast Cancer Cell-Derived Soluble CD44 Promotes Tumor Progression by Triggering Macrophage IL1β Production

lr_support.note: Supports the CD44 side of an SPP1-CD44 macrophage-tumor communication axis through breast-cancer CD44-driven macrophage activation.

papers.evidence_summary: Breast-cancer-derived soluble CD44 activated macrophages to produce IL1β and promoted tumor progression, showing a concrete tumor-to-macrophage communication mechanism centered on CD44.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Provides mechanistic support for CD44-centered tumor-macrophage crosstalk in the breast tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: SPP1+ macrophages in HR+ breast cancer are associated with tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes

lr_support.note: Supports the SPP1-producing macrophage state that commonly mediates SPP1-CD44 signaling in tumors.

papers.evidence_summary: HR-positive breast tumors contained SPP1-positive macrophages associated with tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte patterns, strengthening the relevance of SPP1 macrophage states in breast-cancer CCI.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds an SPP1-high macrophage compartment adjacent to tumor and lymphocyte programs.

papers.title: Expression of VEGFR-1 (Flt-1) in breast cancer is associated with VEGF expression and with node-negative tumour stage

lr_support.note: Directly links VEGF and VEGFR1/Flt1 expression in breast cancer.

papers.evidence_summary: Breast tumors expressing VEGFR1/Flt1 were associated with VEGF expression, supporting a VEGFA-FLT1 signaling axis relevant to angiogenesis and tumor-endothelial communication.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Provides direct pair-level support for the VEGFA-FLT1 axis in breast cancer.

papers.title: TGF-beta receptor type-2 expression in cancer-associated fibroblasts regulates breast cancer cell growth and survival and is a prognostic marker in pre-menopausal breast cancer

lr_support.note: Supports the receptor arm of the TGFβ1-TGFBR2 axis in breast-cancer CAFs.

papers.evidence_summary: CAF-specific TGFBR2 expression was tied to breast cancer cell growth, survival, and prognosis, demonstrating that stromal TGFβ receptor signaling shapes tumor behavior.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds a stromal/CAF-centered TGFβ signaling program around the proliferative tumor compartment.

papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblast spatial heterogeneity and EMILIN1 expression in the tumor microenvironment modulate TGF-β activity and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in breast cancer

lr_support.note: Supports TGFβ activity in spatially organized CAF niches linked to immune exclusion.

papers.evidence_summary: Integrated single-cell and spatial data showed that spatially organized CAF populations modulate TGFβ activity and CD8 T-cell infiltration in breast tumors.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Directly links stromal spatial structure, TGFβ signaling, and T-cell exclusion in a breast-cancer setting.

papers.title: TGF-β1 promotes human breast cancer angiogenesis and malignant behavior by regulating endothelial-mesenchymal transition

lr_support.note: Supports ligand-driven TGFβ1 signaling in a breast-cancer angiogenesis program involving endothelial transition.

papers.evidence_summary: TGFβ1 promoted breast cancer angiogenesis and malignant behavior by inducing endothelial-mesenchymal transition; the study also connects TAM-derived cues with TGFβ and Notch signaling in endothelial cells.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Supports a TGFβ-driven tumor-endothelial crosstalk program around angiogenesis and invasion.

papers.title: An overview on Estrogen receptors signaling and its ligands in breast cancer
papers.evidence_summary: This review summarizes ERα, ERβ, and GPER signaling, including genomic and non-genomic estrogen pathways that drive breast cancer growth and therapy resistance.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds the Estrogen pathway enrichment detected in the Factor3-associated breast cancer program.

papers.title: Crosstalk between PRLR and EGFR/HER2 Signaling Pathways in Breast Cancer
papers.evidence_summary: The review synthesizes PRLR crosstalk with EGFR/HER2 signaling in breast cancer and highlights downstream MAPK and PI3K/Akt signaling relevant to tumor growth and therapy response.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Provides pathway-level support for the EGFR/HER2 and downstream MAPK/PI3K signals highlighted in the analysis context.

papers.title: Molecular Insights on Signaling Cascades in Breast Cancer: A Comprehensive Review
papers.evidence_summary: This review places EGFR, ER, MAPK, and PI3K/Akt signaling inside the broader breast tumor microenvironment and explicitly links these cascades to stromal, immune, and tumor-cell interplay.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Useful umbrella citation for pathway-factor results that intersect tumor, stromal, and immune compartments.

papers.title: NF-κB signaling pathway in tumor microenvironment
papers.evidence_summary: The review describes NF-κB as a core microenvironmental signaling hub that shapes inflammatory signaling, immune-cell behavior, and stromal-tumor interactions.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds the NFkB pathway enrichment even when the supporting breast-cancer paper is pathway-level rather than pair-specific.

papers.title: Hypoxia-driven angiogenesis in breast cancer mechanisms and therapeutic targets: a narrative review
papers.evidence_summary: This review centers breast-cancer hypoxia as a driver of angiogenesis and explains how hypoxic signaling reshapes the tumor microenvironment through VEGF-centered vascular programs.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds the Hypoxia and VEGF pathway hits in spatial tumor regions likely under vascular and oxygen stress.

papers.title: Breast cancer cells-derived Von Willebrand Factor promotes VEGF-A-related angiogenesis through PI3K/Akt-miR-205-5p signaling pathway
papers.evidence_summary: Breast-cancer-cell-derived vWF increased VEGF-A production and vascular proliferation through PI3K/Akt signaling, providing direct experimental support for VEGF and PI3K/Akt coupling in angiogenesis.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Helps explain pathway-factor enrichment around VEGF and PI3K/Akt in tumor-endothelial communication.

papers.title: A trispecific antibody targeting HER2 and T cells inhibits breast cancer growth via CD4 cells
papers.evidence_summary: In HER2-positive breast cancer, CD4 T cells were shown to mediate antitumor effects and induce pro-inflammatory signaling, demonstrating that CD4 T cells can be functional effectors in breast tumor control.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Provides breast-cancer-specific support for a CD4 T-cell compartment interacting with HER2-positive tumor programs.

papers.title: Prognostic value of CD8+ tumor-infiltrating T cells in patients with breast cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.evidence_summary: Across 14 studies, high CD8 T-cell infiltration was associated with better survival in breast cancer, confirming the clinical relevance of CD8-rich tumor microenvironments.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Grounds the CD8 T-cell compartment as a meaningful cell-type feature when interpreting spatial immune neighborhoods.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis reveals immune microenvironment changes and insights into the transition from DCIS to IDC with associated prognostic genes
papers.evidence_summary: Single-cell analysis of the DCIS-to-IDC transition identified immune-microenvironment remodeling, including T-cell proportion changes, across pre-invasive and invasive breast disease.
papers.relevance_to_analysis: Supports mapping the repo's DCIS and invasive-tumor labels onto a literature-backed progression axis.

provenance.curation_method: manual PubMed search and abstract-level relevance screening
